title: Template-free exponential amplification of arbitrary peptides

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 10, Protein amplification chain reaction. Target: in a single pot, exponentially amplify arbitrary peptides into full-length, sequence-faithful copies from amino-acid monomers without a nucleic-acid template; at least 1000-fold increase in abundance with at least 90% per-residue accuracy, without explicit sequencing or reverse translation. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Protein amplification chain reaction
page.definition: Peptides—chains of amino acids—are copied from amino-acid monomers in one reaction mixture, with input sequences directing new covalently linked copies. The copies sustain exponential amplification without DNA or RNA encoding.

goal.need: In 2015, Swaminathan and colleagues described sequence-discriminating protein measurements with typical attomole-to-femtomole sensitivities, or 10⁻¹⁸–10⁻¹⁵ mol. They identified the absence of protein amplification as a constraint on proteome analysis. The motivation for sequence-preserving amplification is to increase the peptide material available for measurement.

statements.quote: Demonstrate exponential amplification of arbitrary peptide substrates.

statements.body: Marcotte laboratory, University of Texas at Austin
statements.quote: Unlike the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for nucleic acids, no methods exist for template-directed amplification of proteins.
statements.context: The protein-sequencing developers identify this limitation while motivating methods for measuring individual peptide molecules.

completion.title: A pooled panel of 100 random peptides passes the protein amplification challenge.
completion.criterion: Preregister, synthesize and pool at least 100 random peptide sequences, each at least 50 residues long. Demonstrate exponential, input-dependent, one-pot synthesis of full-length covalent copies from amino-acid monomers, with at least 1000-fold amplification and at least 90% per-residue accuracy. Exclude nucleic-acid templates, preformed cognate scaffolds, explicit peptide sequencing and reverse translation through nucleic acids. Analytical modifications are permitted only if inactive during amplification.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, problem 10.
completion.threshold_quote: amplified at least 1000x with at least 90% sequence accuracy on a per-residue basis.
completion.basis: This is the originating challenge's explicit acceptance criterion, covering substrate diversity, chain length, amplification and sequence fidelity.

milestones.title: A peptide accelerates formation of covalent copies of itself from peptide fragments.
milestones.criterion: Adding the peptide product increases its own rate of covalent formation from shorter fragments. Published on 8 August 1996, Lee and colleagues demonstrated this for one designed 32-residue helical peptide assembled from 15- and 17-residue fragments. Its growth was parabolic.
milestones.set_by: Chemical self-replication convention, applied by Ghadiri's group in Nature (1996); the published demonstration concerns a designed helical peptide.
milestones.threshold_quote: can act autocatalytically in templating its own synthesis by accelerating the thioester-promoted amide-bond condensation of 15- and 17-residue fragments

milestones.title: A peptide-based chemical replicator exhibits first-order replication kinetics.
milestones.criterion: With precursor concentration approximately constant, replication rate is proportional to replicator abundance: reaction order r = 1. Published on 17 June 2015, one peptide-functionalized disulfide macrocycle gave r = 0.996 ± 0.166 (SD), using four seed concentrations and 3–4 measurements per concentration. The authors could not exclude sub-exponential growth from these measurements alone; their mechanistic model gave r = 1.000. The experiment assembles disulfide rings from peptide-bearing precursors.
milestones.set_by: Chemical self-replication convention, explicitly stated by Colomb-Delsuc and colleagues in Nature Communications (2015); their experiment concerns peptide-functionalized macrocycles.
milestones.threshold_quote: Exponential growth occurs only when the order in autocatalyst is 1.

milestones.title: A peptide template directs three sequence-selective amino-acid additions.
milestones.criterion: Published on 16 January 2018, Rout and colleagues demonstrated three amino-acid additions to a five-residue substrate in an amyloid, an ordered peptide aggregate. An eight-residue product had the specified sequence and stereochemistry among 64 possible triple-addition products. The study examined four template/substrate pairs; experiments were not systematically replicated. This benchmark extends an existing chain using a complementary peptide scaffold.
milestones.set_by: Rout, Friedmann, Riek and Greenwald, Nature Communications (2018), experimental benchmark for alternating amyloid-forming peptides.
milestones.threshold_quote: Here, we report that amyloids composed of short peptides can direct the sequence-selective, regioselective and stereoselective condensation of amino acids.

milestones.title: A pool of ≥100 random peptides is copied exponentially with ≥90% per-residue accuracy.
milestones.criterion: All completion conditions hold, including the ≥100-sequence pool, ≥50-residue length, exponential growth and ≥90% per-residue accuracy, except that ≥1000-fold amplification has not been established.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches of the challenge, peptide self-replication papers and peptide-amplification roadmaps found no published penultimate test. This interim test relaxes only amplification magnitude.

not_found: Searches found no externally specified penultimate criterion for monomer-fed amplification of arbitrary peptide sequences.
No published demonstration satisfying completion or the Atlas penultimate test was found through 14 November 2026.
The challenge does not specify a kinetic fitting rule, a random-sequence sampling scheme, or whether gain and accuracy thresholds apply separately to each sequence or to pooled averages.
The accessible abstract of Lee and colleagues does not state experimental replicate counts.

results.finding: Peptide-functionalized disulfide macrocycle, four seed concentrations with 3–4 measurements each: r = 0.996 ± 0.166 SD.
results.detail: Food concentration was approximately constant during initial growth. The authors could not exclude sub-exponential growth from the measurements alone; their mechanistic simulation gave r = 1.000.
results.quote:
The resulting plot of the initial rate of
replication versus hexamer seed concentration is shown in Fig. 2,
which allowed us to determine a value for the order in replicator r
of 0.996 ±0.166.

results.finding: Four template/substrate pairs were studied; one produced a sequence- and stereoselective triple-addition product.
results.detail: The five-residue substrate was extended using a complementary peptide scaffold. The initial substrate/template mixture was soluble; the desired product was detected in the insoluble fraction. Experiments were not systematically replicated.
results.quote:
Of
the 64 possible triple addition products, only three could be
detected in the insoluble fraction: two major products L-(FR) 4
and L-FF(FR) 3 and a minor product of undetermined stereo-
chemistry, however most likely fFFRFRFR-NH2 in which the ﬁnal
addition is a D-phenylalanine.
